explanations.explanation: Towns it is, friend. Solomon, Israel's king, gave twenty towns in the land of Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who had supplied him with cedar and cypress logs and gold. Most folks hand over a gift card. Solomon handed over a whole map.

Ships do show up in this passage, but not as a gift. Solomon assembles a fleet at Ezion-geber later on, in verse 26. The gift to Hiram king of Tyre, the man who supplied the cedar, cypress and gold, was twenty towns in the land of Galilee.

Chariots are in the passage, friend, but they're parked somewhere else. Solomon has store cities for his chariots and horses, back in verse 19. What he gave Hiram king of Tyre was twenty towns in the land of Galilee, no horsepower included.

I get why you'd think so, since twenty towns sounds like a great present. But the text says Hiram went out from Tyre to inspect them and was not pleased with them. He asks, “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?” That's a long way from a happy dance.

That's right. Hiram king of Tyre went out to inspect the towns, and the text says he was not pleased with them. His own words are, “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?” Twenty towns, and he still wasn't pleased.

explanations.answer: The non-Israelites still in the land
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. Solomon conscripted the descendants of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, the people who were not Israelites and who remained in the land. The Israelites had been unable to devote them to destruction. The text says they were forced laborers "…to this day."

Egypt is in the passage, but not for this. Pharaoh king of Egypt shows up because he captured Gezer and gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife. The text names the forced laborers as the people remaining in the land who were not Israelites. It doesn't say anything about captives from Egypt.

Edom only comes up as a location, friend. Ezion-geber, where Solomon assembles his fleet, is near Eloth in Edom. For the forced labor, the text points to the people who remained of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites. It says nothing about prisoners from Edom.

explanations.answer: They are his men of war and commanders
explanations.explanation: That's the reason the text gives. Solomon did not consign any of the Israelites to slavery, because they were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry. That's a whole leadership roster.

explanations.answer: They pay Solomon a yearly tax
explanations.explanation: No tax is mentioned here, friend. The text says Solomon did not consign any Israelites to slavery, "…because they were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry." That's the reason the verse gives.

explanations.answer: They are needed to farm the land
explanations.explanation: Farming isn't in this verse. The text says the Israelites were Solomon's men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry. That list is the reason Solomon did not consign any of them to slavery.

True, baker. The Israelites were also the chief officers over Solomon's projects, with 550 supervisors over the people who did the work. Those same Israelites were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry. That's a lot of clipboards.

Not this time, friend. The statement is true. The text says the Israelites were also the chief officers over Solomon's projects, 550 supervisors over the people who did the work. Five hundred fifty supervisors. I'd hate to see that group chat.

That's her. As soon as Pharaoh's daughter came up from the City of David to the palace Solomon had built for her, he built the supporting terraces. The text calls her Solomon's wife earlier, back in verse 16. A new palace and then terraces. That's a man who finishes the job.

The queen of Sheba isn't in this passage, friend. The palace in verse 24 was built for Pharaoh's daughter, Solomon's wife, the one Pharaoh king of Egypt gave Gezer to as a dowry. She came up from the City of David to it, and then Solomon built the supporting terraces.

Michal isn't mentioned anywhere in these verses. The text says the palace was for Pharaoh's daughter, who is Solomon's wife. As soon as she came up from the City of David to it, Solomon built the supporting terraces.

Three it is. Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD, burning incense with them before the LORD. The verse closes with "So he completed the temple." Three times a year is a rhythm I could keep on my calendar.

Seven is a fine Bible number, but it's not the one here. The text says three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD. He burned incense with them before the LORD.

Twelve times a year would be far more often than the text says, friend. It says three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD. Then it says he completed the temple.

Right, baker. Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants, sailors who knew the sea, to serve in the fleet with Solomon's servants. Remember, he's the man who supplied the cedar, cypress and gold. That's a king who sends help when a fleet needs sailors.

Pharaoh king of Egypt is in this passage, but for something else. He captured Gezer, set it on fire and gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife. The sailors who knew the sea came from Hiram king of Tyre.

Hadad isn't in this passage, friend. The fleet is at Ezion-geber, near Eloth in Edom, but the text says the sailors came from Hiram king of Tyre. He sent his servants, who knew the sea, to serve with Solomon's servants.

Ophir is the place. Hiram's sailors and Solomon's servants sailed there and imported gold, 420 talents of it, and delivered it to Solomon. Sailing for gold makes me feel small, since I once walked across the counter for a sprinkle and thought I'd done something big.
Cyprus is a real island, but it isn't named here. The text says the fleet sailed to Ophir and imported gold from there, 420 talents, and delivered it to Solomon. Ophir is the place the verse names.
Crete isn't in these verses, friend. The text says Hiram's sailors and Solomon's servants sailed to Ophir. They imported 420 talents of gold from there and delivered it to Solomon.
